<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=summary -->
Spawned by TKT-73 / ADR-025 (admission lifecycle events and offline reconciliation). The ADR's decision statements are binding constraints on this ticket.

<!-- sdlc:stage=ready kind=claim -->
**Claimed** — branch `TKT-86-admission-conflict-alarm` off `origin/main` @ 70f6e48.

**GATELESS RUN — all four human gates waived by explicit repo-owner directive (process experiment).**
The owner is the repo owner and PO, and waived Gates 1–4 for this ticket in the run instruction.
Recorded here so the board history shows this ticket ran without human gates:

| Gate | Normally | This run |
|---|---|---|
| 1 priority | human → Ready | already given (ticket was in Ready) |
| 2 plan approval | human → Building | orchestrator stands in as judge: prefer the critique's recommendation; absent one, the most reversible option. Every self-made decision recorded in `kind=plan-final`. |
| 3 review + merge | human reviews + squash-merges | orchestrator squash-merges after the adversarial ai-review converges (same triage/second-pass/churn-cap rules). Review-guide still posted first, as the audit record. |
| 4 PO acceptance | PO validates COS | orchestrator self-validates each COS against test evidence on the merged code. |

Not waived, and unchanged: `config.models` routing (no substitutions), cross-model review for both
plan and code, TDD with tests observed red first, `make check` green before every push and after the
merge, every marker comment, no AI attribution anywhere.

Per `ab-stages.md` §`plan` item 6, a gate waived by owner directive is **not** `risk:low`: every plan
arm still runs, both are critiqued, and the arm mapping is **disclosed immediately** in the stage
comment (anonymization is moot when the judge launched the arms — the disclosure is the audit
substitute).

**Selection reason.** Owner-directed. Zero open blockers (`links` empty). Sole ticket in flight.

**Shaping debt carried in, stated up front.** TKT-86 has **no `readiness` object and no
context-mémo** — it was spawned as a follow-up by TKT-73 and reached Ready without the 8-item DoR
bake. Nothing to seed the plan brief from, so the governing-ADR list below is resolved from scratch
at claim time against `docs/adr/` @ HEAD (the skill requires re-resolution anyway; here it is the
only resolution). Flagged for the retro.

**Governing ADRs, re-resolved at HEAD** — and what each constrains *for this ticket*:

- **ADR-025 §D6/§D8/§D9/§D10** — the ticket's own source. §D6: every reconciled single-entry
  conflict owes a durable admission-conflict alarm, a class separate from ADR-021's integrity
  alarms. §D8: no gate identity or conflict reason enters the canonical form — **reasons live in the
  alarm payload**. §D9: bounded identifiers and enums only. §D10: one new NATS contract, own
  schema-1, ADR-017 thereafter.
- **ADR-017** — governs the alarm contract's evolution. Bump on **consumer semantics**, not parse
  compatibility; a consumer dispatches on `schema` before decoding `data`; `schema <= 0` is a broken
  envelope, not the future; a fixture built from the type under test cannot fail.
- **ADR-021** — the trust boundary and the append path. An alarm is **visibility, not containment**:
  it proves nothing against a database-write adversary (ADR-025 §Claims says so explicitly). Any
  wording this ticket adds must name its adversary.
- **ADR-003 §D3** — the PII floor the payload must hold.
- **ADR-009 §5** — envelope invariants (`id`/`type`/`schema` stable across variants).

**Scope reality this ticket must resolve first (input to Planning, not a decision made here).**
Most of what the description asks for is **already at HEAD**, landed by siblings that merged after
TKT-86 was written: `services/access/internal/store/reconcile.go` has
`SubjectAdmissionConflictAlarm`, `conflictAlarmData` and `oweConflictAlarm` (transactional, schema 1,
TKT-85), `conflicts.go` has the revisable policy-conflict class the GATE-3 REVIEW ADDITION asks for
(TKT-87), `compose.yaml` creates both operator durables, `main.go` fail-closed boot-checks them, and
`docs/development.md` documents the policy-conflict class. So this is a **delta ticket**, and the
plan stage's first job is to establish that delta honestly against ADR-025 rather than rebuild what
exists. Candidate gaps I saw while resolving the ADRs — offered to the planners as leads, **not** as
scope: (a) §D8 says conflict *reasons* live in the alarm payload and §D9 says *enums* — today's
`conflictAlarmData` carries no reason enum at all; (b) no test pins the envelope's field set against
the PII floor; (c) `docs/development.md` gives the policy-conflict class an operator paragraph and
the plain admission-conflict class none. If the honest delta is empty, saying so with evidence is a
valid outcome.

**Risk.** Not `risk:low` (and `risk:low` is moot under the waiver — it only skips a gate that is
already waived). The area is a signed append path plus a durable outbox committed in the same
transaction. If the plan turns out to need a **migration**, an **auth** change, or a **CI/deploy**
change that neither the ticket nor ADR-025 anticipated, that is a stop-and-report condition under
the owner's instruction, not a call to make in-session.

**Stage routing** (`.claude/sdlc.config.json`): plan = A/B `["gpt-5.6-sol", "opus-4.8"]` ·
planReview = `fable-5` · implement = `main-agent` · aiReview = A/B `["gpt-5.6-sol", "fable-5"]`.
Cross-model invariant checked per arm: planner arms (gpt-5.6-sol, opus-4.8) both ≠ planReview
(fable-5) ✓; implementer (main-agent = Opus 5, this session) ≠ both review arms (gpt-5.6-sol,
fable-5) ✓.

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan -->
## Plan draft — A/B stage, 2 arms

`config.models.plan` is an array, so this stage ran as an A/B per `ab-stages.md`: both arms got the
**same brief**, read-only, launched in parallel. **2× the spend for this stage, stated rather than
hidden.**

**Arm mapping — disclosed immediately** (`ab-stages.md` §`plan` item 6: under an owner-waived Gate 2
the orchestrator *is* the judge, so anonymization is moot and immediate disclosure is the audit
substitute). Ticket 86 is even → first config element is A.

| Arm | Model | Harness | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | `gpt-5.6-sol` | codex — **rung 1 hung, rung 2 delivered** | full plan, 150.3k tokens |
| **B** | `opus-4.8` | headless `claude -p`, read-only | full plan |

**Arm A harness incident (logged as a finding about the harness, per `ab-stages.md`).** Rung 1, the
companion `task --model gpt-5.6-sol --effort high --background`, **hung**: 9h02m elapsed with the log
silent from 04:36Z, killed mid-investigation with no final answer and nothing legible to salvage.
Escalated exactly one rung per `codex-runner.md` — raw `codex exec -m gpt-5.6-sol -s read-only` with
the brief on **stdin** — which completed. This is the **second** ticket where companion
`task --background` hung and raw `exec` succeeded (TKT-56/S4 was the first: status=running 1h29m, log
silent 86m). Two independent occurrences is a pattern, not an anomaly — retro item below.
Also note the model alias: `opus-4.8` is **rejected** by the CLI; the model is reachable as
`claude-opus-4-8`. Same model, canonical id — not a substitution.

### Both arms agree on the shape of the ticket

TKT-86 is a **delta ticket**: its siblings TKT-85 and TKT-87 merged after it was written and already
shipped the substance. Both arms independently verified and both concluded:

- **§D6** (durable alarm, own class, transactional with the append) — **satisfied at HEAD**.
  `reconcile.go:217-233` appends `duplicate_admit` then `oweConflictAlarm` in the same `tx`, one
  commit; subject `platform.access.admission-conflict.alarm` at `:19`; outbox at
  `0003_lifecycle_integrity.sql:199`; durable in `compose.yaml:118-120`; fail-closed boot guard at
  `main.go:199`; pending-depth gauge at `main.go:225`.
- **§D2 GATE-3 REVIEW ADDITION** (derived pass-policy conflicts alarmed as revisable) — **satisfied
  at HEAD**, shipped by TKT-87 (`conflicts.go`, `scan.go:302-390`, `revisable:true`).
- **§D10** (own NATS contract, schema 1) — **satisfied at HEAD**. Both arms independently grepped
  and found **no consumer in this repo** decodes the subject.
- **§D9 PII floor** — payload is PII-free by inspection (4 UUIDs + a timestamp + a bool) but
  **untested**: the existing smoke assertion decodes a **3-field subset**, so an added `buyer_email`
  would pass green. **Both arms call this a real gap.**
- **Operator docs** — `docs/development.md` documents the integrity class and the policy-conflict
  class; the plain admission-conflict class has **no paragraph**. **Both arms call this a real gap.**

Both arms also independently declined the same out-of-scope work: no rebuild of the outbox/durable/
metrics, no `conflicts.go` rework, no migration, no consumer, no canonical-form change, no OpenAPI
change (§D10's HTTP rollout is explicitly assigned to other tickets by the ADR itself).

### Where they split — one real design disagreement

**Does ADR-025 §D8 oblige the admission-conflict payload to carry a `reason` enum?**
§D8: *"no gate identity or conflict reason enters the canonical form; reasons live in the alarm payload."*

- **Arm A (`gpt-5.6-sol`): yes — real §D8 gap.** Reads the clause as relocating the conflict reason
  *into* the alarm payload, and notes §D6 already separates the integrity class, so an
  "integrity-only" reading leaves the sentence with no payload destination. Proposes a bounded
  `reason:"duplicate_admit"` enum, **required**, therefore **schema 2** — arguing ADR-017 §3a
  (old-consumer incorrectness) does *not* fire since there is no consumer, but §3b (a required field
  the current arm cannot validate without rejecting legal schema-1 payloads) fires independently.
  4 files, incl. a behaviour-preserving extraction of the envelope marshalling into a pure builder.
- **Arm B (`opus-4.8`): no — refuted.** Reads §D8 as a constraint *on the canonical form* (keep
  reasons out of the signed trail), not a mandate that every alarm enumerate reasons. Notes the class
  that *has* reasons — policy conflicts — already carries its `Rule` enum in its payload, so the
  sentence is already true where it applies; and that the admission-conflict class has exactly **one**
  condition (§D2 scopes `duplicate_admit` to single-entry tickets), so **the subject is the reason** —
  there is no reason space to enumerate. 2 files, test + docs, **no source change**.

Second-order split: **test seam**. Arm A wants a pure envelope-*builder* seam (requires extracting
one from `oweConflictAlarm`) so the test pins the top-level envelope keys too. Arm B wants a pure
test marshalling `conflictAlarmData` directly, arguing the PII surface is `data` alone and the
top-level keys are ADR-009 §5 invariants already asserted by the smoke test — and that extracting a
builder is a refactor of a live schema-1 path for zero PII benefit.

Both arms independently identified the ADR-017 **fixture trap** and both avoid it the same way:
assert **negative closure** (exact key set) against a **hand-written literal allow-list**, never a
set derived from the struct under test.

Full arm texts are in the run's scratchpad; the sections above reproduce every load-bearing claim.
Next: `fable-5` critiques **both** arms as `planReview`, then the selection and every self-made Gate-2
decision land in `kind=plan-final`.

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan-final -->
## Plan final — delta on the `kind=plan` draft

**The `kind=plan` draft, arm B, as amended below, is the plan.** This comment is the delta, not a
restatement — read it together with the draft comment above.

### Selection — arm B wins, arm A contributes two grafts

`planReview` = **`fable-5`** critiqued **both** arms (per `ab-stages.md` item 6 under a waived Gate 2).
Its recommendation: **arm B (`opus-4.8`) is the spine; arm A (`gpt-5.6-sol`) must not proceed as-is.**
Grafted from arm A: its exact-key COS discipline (COS-3 was the best-stated assertion in either draft)
and an explicit ADR-017 posture note for future evolution.

**Arm A's rejection is not a close call, and I verified the decisive fact myself rather than taking
the critic's word for it:** arm A proposed bumping this contract to schema 2, listed four files to
touch, and wrote *"final diff is limited to the four paths below"* — but
`smoke/multi_event_admission_test.go:468` hard-asserts `admission-conflict alarm schema == 1`, and
that file is **not** among the four. `Makefile:17` → `scripts/smoke.sh:190-199` runs that module in
the gate. **Arm A's plan mechanically fails `make check` as written.** Confirmed at HEAD by reading
the file. Arm A had cited `scripts/smoke.sh:96` to prove its *store-package* test would run in the
gate, while missing that the *same script* runs the `smoke/` module that pins schema 1 — the
"couldn't run the gate, so mis-sized the blast radius" failure the pre-mortem pass exists to catch.

### Gate-2 decisions I made myself (gate waived by owner directive)

Rule I applied, from the run instruction: **prefer the option the critique recommends; absent a
recommendation, the most reversible option.** Here every decision had an explicit critique
recommendation, so the tie-break rule was never needed — and in each case the recommended option is
also the more reversible one, which is worth stating because it means the waiver cost nothing.

**D1 — Does ADR-025 §D8 oblige a `reason` enum in the payload? → NO. Rejected.**
Critique's verdict, adopted. §D8's sentence (`ADR-025:190-191`) is a routing constraint **on the
canonical form** — keep reasons out of the signed trail — not a mandate that every alarm class
enumerate reasons. The class that *has* a reason space is the derived policy-conflict class, and it
already carries its `Rule` enum in its payload (`scan.go:311,376`), so the sentence is already true
where it applies. Decisive engineering point, which is mine to underline: the admission-conflict
class has **exactly one** condition (§D2 scopes `duplicate_admit` to single-entry tickets), and arm
A's own proposed value was `reason:"duplicate_admit"` — a constant equal to the event type, on a
subject whose name already says it. **A field with one possible value carries zero information.**
Reversibility: adding a field later is easy; removing one from a shipped contract is not.

**D2 — Bump to schema 2? → NO. Contract stays schema 1.** Moot once D1 is rejected. Recorded because
arm A's *conditional* logic was sound and should not be lost: a **required** field the schema-1 arm
cannot validate does fire ADR-017 §3b independently of §3a, even with zero consumers. The conditional
never triggers because the field isn't owed. Verified independently: no consumer in this repo decodes
this subject — only the producer, the compose durable, the boot guard/metrics, and tests.

**D3 — Test seam → the persisted envelope bytes in the store smoke test, not a struct.** This is the
critique's amendment and it overrides *both* arms. Arm B's pure test marshals `conflictAlarmData`,
which pins `data` only; the envelope top level is an anonymous inline struct in `oweConflictAlarm`
(`reconcile.go:311-317`) that no pure test can reach, so a PII field added *there* stays invisible.
Arm B dismissed the smoke seam as "no extra PII teeth" — that is wrong, and I agree with the critic:
asserting exact key sets on the **persisted outbox bytes** pins both levels and binds the claim to
what is actually emitted rather than to a struct the producer merely happens to use today.

**D4 — Also keep arm B's optional pure test? → NO. One assertion, not two.** The critique marks it
"optional, cheap". The smoke-side assertion **strictly dominates** it — same `data` closure, plus the
top level, plus real emitted bytes — so a second test would buy only a faster red/green loop at the
cost of a second thing to keep in sync. Fewest seams is the standing preference. Reversible: if the
fast loop is ever wanted, `conflicts_test.go` is the pure-test precedent in this package and adding
one is minutes.

**D5 — Extend the existing test or add a sibling? → Extend
`TestReconcileConflictAppendsDuplicateAdmitAndOwesAlarm`.** It already fetches the envelope
(`occurrence_smoke_test.go:412-413`); a sibling test would re-pay ~40 lines of PostgreSQL setup to
assert on the same row. Extending with a named helper keeps the intent legible.

### Amendments to the arm-B draft

1. **Replace** arm B's `TestConflictAlarmPayloadPIIFloor` (pure, `data`-only, new
   `reconcile_test.go`) **with** an exact-key closure assertion inside the existing smoke test —
   both envelope levels, on the persisted bytes. (D3, D4, D5.)
2. **Accept** arm B's §D6/§D8/§D10 "satisfied at HEAD" verdicts and its whole Skipped list.
3. **Accept** arm B's §D9 verdict ("satisfied in code; untested against the floor"), reworded per D3
   to be about emitted bytes rather than the struct.
4. **Reject** arm A's §D9 grade: it counted the "missing enum" as a §D9 gap, but §D9's enum language
   is a **ceiling** ("bounded identifiers and enums *only*"), not a floor mandating one exist — it
   double-counted its §D8 inference into §D9 to widen the delta.
5. **Add** to the docs paragraph one sentence closing the reason question in writing (see below), so
   it is settled on the record instead of re-litigated next ticket.

### The plan

**COS** (proposed here — the ticket reached Ready with none):
1. The persisted admission-conflict alarm envelope has **exactly** the top-level keys
   `{id, type, occurred_at, schema, data}` and **exactly** the data keys
   `{alarm_id, organizer_id, ticket_id, occurrence_id, device_occurred_at, skew_flagged}` — no
   undeclared field can enter without failing the gate (ADR-025 §D9 PII floor).
2. The contract remains `platform.access.admission-conflict.alarm` at **schema 1**; no bump, no
   payload change, no migration.
3. Operators have an in-repo paragraph for the admission-conflict class: subject, schema, durable
   (`ACCESS_ADMISSION_CONFLICT_DURABLE`), fail-closed boot guard, the retained-not-read caveat, and
   the ADR-025 §Claims adversary boundary quoted verbatim.
4. No regression: `make check` green; §D6/§D8/§D10 behaviour untouched, proven by the existing suite
   staying green unmodified.

**Files** (2):
- `services/access/internal/store/occurrence_smoke_test.go` — extend
  `TestReconcileConflictAppendsDuplicateAdmitAndOwesAlarm` with exact-key closure at both envelope
  levels, via a small named helper. Hand-written literal allow-lists.
- `docs/development.md` — one admission-conflict operator paragraph next to the policy-conflict one
  (~:191).

**Zero source lines change.** No `reconcile.go`, no migration, no consumer, no OpenAPI/codegen, no ADR.

**Test plan.** The assertion is **negative closure** — sorted key set *equals* a hand-written literal
— not a subset check. That is what defeats the ADR-017 fixture trap: only the *actual* side comes
from production; the *expected* side is written independently, so a new field cannot smuggle itself
into the expectation. The existing assertion at `occurrence_smoke_test.go:419-431` decodes a 3-field
**subset**, which is the exact anti-pattern being fixed. **Observed-red discipline:** this is a guard
on unchanged behaviour, so it is green at HEAD by construction; teeth are proven by temporarily
adding a junk field to `conflictAlarmData`, watching it go red, and reverting. That run gets recorded
in the PR description, per the critique — an unverifiable "observed red" claim is worth nothing.

**Pre-mortem lens** (applied by `fable-5`; 5 causes). What it changed: the seam moved from struct to
persisted bytes (cause 3), and the docs paragraph gained the reason-question sentence (cause 1). It
also caught the schema-2 gate break (cause 2), which killed arm A. Causes 4 (docs drifting toward a
containment claim — mitigated by quoting `ADR-025:236-237` verbatim) and 5 (unverifiable observed-red
— mitigated in the PR description) are handled above.

### ⚠ Introduced at plan-review, reviewed by no second model

Cross-model review covers the draft and (later) the code — **not** plan-review's own inventions.
Two design elements here were *added* by `fable-5` rather than accepted/amended/rejected from either
draft, and reach Gate 2 reviewed by nobody but their author:

1. **Asserting exact key closure on the persisted envelope bytes at both levels** (D3). Neither arm
   proposed this: arm B pinned the struct's `data` only; arm A wanted the top level pinned but via
   extracting a pure builder from a live path. The smoke-bytes route is the critic's own synthesis.
   *My check:* the bytes exist and are already fetched at `occurrence_smoke_test.go:412-413`, so the
   assertion needs no new machinery — verified by reading the file, not inferred.
2. **The docs sentence closing the reason question for the future** — that this class is
   single-condition, the subject is the reason, and a future reason space is an ADR-017 §3 decision
   on this contract. Offered by the critic as a "third option neither arm proposed".

Both are low-risk (a test assertion and a documentation sentence — no runtime path), which is why I
accepted them without a further review round. Named again here so Gate 3 sees them.

### Risks / stop-and-report posture

None of the run's stop conditions are triggered: no auth, no money path, no migration, no CI/deploy
change. Diff is one test file and one doc file. If implementation unexpectedly needs a source change
in `reconcile.go`, that is a signal the §D8 decision was wrong — stop and report rather than quietly
widening scope.

Transitioning **Planning → Building** myself under the owner's Gate-2 waiver.

<!-- sdlc:stage=coding kind=summary -->
## Implementation — TDD, gate green, PR open

```yaml
stage: coding
implementer: main-agent (Opus 5) — per config.models.implement, no delegation
commit: 8157f92
pr: https://github.com/mathd/ticketing_system/pull/110
diff: 2 files, +44/-0 test, +25/-1 docs — zero source lines
gate: make check — EXIT=0, log body swept for 'Error N|FAIL|drifted|make: ***|panic:', no hits
```

**Built exactly the amended arm-B plan.** No deviations, no discoveries that changed the shape — the
stop-and-report condition I named in `plan-final` (needing a `reconcile.go` source change, which
would have meant the §D8 decision was wrong) did **not** trigger. Source is untouched.

### Files

- `services/access/internal/store/occurrence_smoke_test.go` — `assertConflictAlarmPIIFloor` helper
  plus one call site inside the existing
  `TestReconcileConflictAppendsDuplicateAdmitAndOwesAlarm`. Exact-key closure on the **persisted
  outbox envelope**, both levels, against hand-written literals.
- `docs/development.md` — the admission-conflict operator paragraph, next to the policy-conflict one.

### TDD — observed red, both branches, before it landed

The assertion guards behaviour that is already correct, so it is green at HEAD **by construction**.
An unverified "observed red" claim on a guard like this is worth nothing, so the teeth were proven
by breaking the payload once per literal and reverting:

| Branch | Injected | Observed |
|---|---|---|
| data level | `BuyerEmail string \`json:"buyer_email"\`` on `conflictAlarmData` | FAIL — `conflict alarm data keys = [alarm_id buyer_email …], want exactly [alarm_id device_occurred_at …]` |
| envelope level | `ScannerOp string \`json:"scanner_operator"\`` on the inline envelope struct | FAIL — `conflict alarm envelope keys = [data id occurred_at scanner_operator schema type], want exactly [data id occurred_at schema type]` |

Both reverted (`git checkout reconcile.go`), then the **full** access store smoke package green
(`ok … 9.189s`), then the full gate. The second injection matters: the envelope top level is the
half arm B's struct-level test could not have reached, so proving that literal separately is what
makes the critique's amendment worth having rather than a claim.

### Gate discipline

`make check` run as the **sole** command in its shell call, redirected to a file, exit code written
to a separate sentinel — no chaining, no pipe, no `pgrep` polling. It ran as a background job, so
PASS was judged from the **log body** (swept for `Error [0-9]+|FAIL|drifted|make: \*\*\*|panic:` —
zero hits) and not from the harness-reported exit code, per the TKT-101 divergence. Both agreed here.
Then `git push`, then `gh pr create` — never chained onto the gate.

Note: `gh pr create` warned "2 uncommitted changes". Those are the two pre-existing untracked paths
that were in the tree at claim time (`.antigravitycli/`, a stray `.DS_Store`) — not mine, not staged,
not in the diff.

Next: `agent:ai-review` — A/B adversarial review, arms `gpt-5.6-sol` and `fable-5`, each primed for
guilt and given the diff only.

<!-- sdlc:stage=ai-review kind=summary -->
## Adversarial review — A/B first pass + two convergence passes

`config.models.aiReview` is an array, so the **first** pass ran as an A/B: both arms on the same
diff, each primed for guilt, **each given the diff only** — neither got the plan or the reasoning.
**2× the spend for that stage, stated not hidden.** Second and third passes ran on the **control arm
only** (`gpt-5.6-sol`, first array element) — second passes are never A/B'd, since arms would be
scoring different diffs.

| Pass | Scope | Arms | Findings |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `8157f92` vs base | **A/B**: `gpt-5.6-sol` (codex raw exec) + `fable-5` (subagent) | 7 deduped |
| 2 | fix diff `8157f92..e755f2b` | control only | 3 |
| 3 | fix diff `e755f2b..474476b` | control only | **0 — clean** |

### Arm tally, first pass (deduped by defect, every arm that found it credited)

| Arm | Confirmed | Unique-confirmed | Refuted |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gpt-5.6-sol` | 5 | 3 (K3, K4, K5) | 0 |
| `fable-5` | 4 | 2 (K6, K7) | 0 |

Neither arm produced a false positive. Different shapes: `gpt-5.6-sol` was stronger on **claims** —
it caught all three documentation defects, including the one `fable-5` explicitly cleared.
`fable-5` was stronger on **mechanism** — it alone stated the blocking bypass in its general form,
and it did the deepest verification work (compiled and linted under the gate's build tag, ran both
affected tests against a throwaway PostgreSQL, grepped every doc fact individually).

### Per-finding verdicts — nothing silently dropped

| # | Finding | Arms | Verdict | Action |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| K1 | `,omitempty` field is absent from any fixture that leaves it zero → key-set pin cannot fail | B (general), A (skew-scoped) | **CONFIRMED — blocking** | Fixed: pin json tags at the source, where the fixture has no say |
| K2 | Keys pinned, values not — PII can hide inside an allowed key | A + B | **CONFIRMED** | Fixed: decode every value into its contracted scalar |
| K3 | Skew-flagged conflict is a second emitted variant, never asserted | A only | **CONFIRMED** | Fixed: assertion applied there too |
| K4 | "the admission cannot be recorded without the alarm being owed" — unscoped atomicity claim | A only | **CONFIRMED** | Fixed: scoped to the honest path, database writer named |
| K5 | Payload inventory said "identifiers and one boolean", omitting the timestamp | A only | **CONFIRMED** | Fixed |
| K6 | Doc contrasted with the policy class using `reason`; that class's field is `rule` (`reason` is the *integrity* class's) | B only | **CONFIRMED** | Fixed |
| K7 | `RequireAlarmRoute` names `ACCESS_LIFECYCLE_ALARM_DURABLE` in the error for all three classes | B only | **CONFIRMED — pre-existing on `origin/main`** | **INCIDENTAL → TKT-119** |
| P1 | `null` satisfies every scalar decode — `encoding/json` leaves the target untouched | control (pass 2) | **CONFIRMED — important** | Fixed: reject null, pin field types |
| P2 | Doc claimed both levels decoded; only the six data values were | control (pass 2) | **CONFIRMED** | Fixed: envelope values decoded too, `type` asserted equal to the subject |
| P3 | ADR-025 §D9 says "identifiers and enums only" but §D5 mandates the timestamp the payload carries | control (pass 2) | **CONFIRMED — pre-existing** | **INCIDENTAL → TKT-120** |

### Why three passes, and why that is convergence rather than churn

The cap is two passes per **stable** diff; **a pass that invalidates the previous pass's fix resets
the counter** (absolute cap 4). Pass 2 did exactly that: it proved pass 1's value-decoding fix wrong
**at the root** — `null` unmarshals into `uuid.UUID`, `time.Time` and `bool` without error, so every
scalar decode pass 1 added could be satisfied by a null and proved nothing. That is not a nit about
pass 1's fix; it is that fix not working. The structural response (reject null + pin Go types) then
became the branch's least-reviewed, riskiest commit, which is precisely the case the rule says to
review once more. Pass 3 found **nothing**, so the diff is stable and the loop is closed — no fourth
pass, and no fix diff is left unreviewed.

Each pass raised **new** defects; none re-litigated a triaged one and none shrank into style. That is
the difference between converging and churning.

### Verification discipline

Every finding was checked against the **revision under review**, not the base — `origin/main` was
used only to establish that K7 and P3 pre-existed the change (both do; that is why they were
deferred rather than fixed here). Both new guards were proven by **injection** before landing, not
asserted: a `guest_ref,omitempty` field (passed the wire pin, caught at the source — the exact
bypass), an `organizer_id` carrying an operator email inside the allowed key, and a nil
`*struct` `organizer_id` marshalling as `null`.

One caveat I am labelling as my own: all three codex passes reported that the read-only sandbox
blocked Go from creating its build directory, so **none of them compiled the code**. `fable-5` did
compile, vet and lint it under the smoke tag. Beyond that, the compile/lint/test evidence is mine —
`make check` green on each of the three commits, judged from the log body.

### learnings:

1. **The codex companion's `task --background` hangs; raw `codex exec` does not. Second occurrence,
   same shape — this is now a pattern.** Here: 9h02m elapsed, log silent from 04:36Z, killed
   mid-investigation with no final answer and nothing salvageable. TKT-56/S4 was the first
   (status=running 1h29m, log silent 86m). Both times rung 2 (raw `codex exec -m gpt-5.6-sol
   -s read-only`, prompt on stdin) completed normally. → **`docs/learnings/`** (repo house), and it
   is already partly in `references/codex-runner.md`; what is new is that it has now happened twice,
   which turns "known failure shape" into "expect it". *Concrete:* add the second occurrence and a
   recommended wall-clock kill threshold (~20 min of log silence) to the runner reference's
   escalation section.
2. **`opus-4.8` is not a valid model id to the CLI; `claude-opus-4-8` is.** Cost one failed probe.
   → **process/config house**: the sdlc config's model strings and the CLI's accepted aliases are
   different vocabularies, and the config's value must be *resolvable*, not just recognisable to a
   human. *Concrete:* note the canonical id next to the arm in `.claude/sdlc.config.json`, or
   validate arm ids at claim time the way `governingAdrs` are already validated against real files.
3. **`encoding/json` treats `null` as "leave the target untouched" for `uuid.UUID`, `time.Time` and
   `bool` alike — so a scalar-decode assertion that does not reject `null` explicitly proves
   nothing.** This defeated an entire review round's fix. It generalises well beyond this contract:
   any "the value must be a bounded scalar" test in this repo has the same hole. → **technical
   standards house** (`docs/learnings/`). *Concrete:* one short learning note, because the next
   person writing a payload-shape assertion will reach for `json.Unmarshal` into a typed target and
   inherit the bug.
4. **A guard against *conditional* emission cannot live in a fixture.** A `,omitempty` field is
   absent from any fixture that leaves it zero, so no wire-level assertion can see it — the fixture
   is what decides whether the field appears. The check has to move to the source (tags + field
   types via reflection). This is a sharper, more actionable statement of the ADR-017 fixture trap
   than "don't build fixtures from the type under test". → **technical standards house**, same note
   as (3).
5. **Sibling tickets silently consume each other's scope.** TKT-86 was written before TKT-85 and
   TKT-87 merged, and they delivered ~90% of it. Nothing on the board reflected that; only reading
   the code at claim time revealed it. → **process house**. *Concrete:* when a ticket's siblings
   from the same ADR merge first, re-verify the parent's scope before claiming — making
   "delta against the ADR at HEAD" the plan's first deliverable worked well here and is worth making
   standard for any ADR-spawned follow-up.

### retro:

**(1) What would have made this ticket faster or better?**

- **The missing shaping is the top item.** TKT-86 reached `Ready` with **no `readiness` object and
  no context-mémo** — it was spawned by TKT-73 and never went through the 8-item DoR bake. The board
  is supposed to hard-block Gate 1 while any `readiness` item is `open`; here there was no
  `readiness` field at all, so there was nothing to block on. **An absent field passed a check
  designed to fail on an incomplete one.** That is a real hole, not a one-off oversight, and it cost
  the whole governing-ADR resolution being done from scratch at claim time.
  *Concrete:* `local-tracker.md` / the board's Gate-1 guard should treat a **missing** `readiness`
  object as failing, identically to an `open` item.
- **The 9h hang should have been caught in minutes.** I launched the arm and only polled it later;
  the log had been silent for hours by then. Nothing in the runner reference gives a silence
  threshold. *Concrete:* `references/codex-runner.md` — state an explicit kill rule (log mtime
  silent > ~20 min ⇒ kill and escalate a rung), so the ladder is time-bounded and not just
  attempt-bounded.
- **The scope-already-delivered discovery was luck, not process.** I found it because I read the
  code before writing the claim. A run that trusted the ticket text would have rebuilt shipped work
  or, worse, "fixed" it. Making the ADR-delta the plan's first deliverable is what saved it —
  worth generalising (learning 5).

**(2) What should the humans change?**

- **Decide whether the gateless mode is a keeper, using this ticket's numbers.** Human wait was
  ~1 minute and the output survived three adversarial passes — but the honest counter-evidence is

  those two is the thing to fix — Gate 2 had a real adversary, Gate 3 did not.
- **Shape ADR-spawned follow-ups when the ADR lands, not later.** TKT-86, TKT-85 and TKT-87 all came
  out of ADR-025; only TKT-86 skipped the bake, and it is the one that went stale.
- **`.claude/sdlc.config.json` should carry resolvable model ids** (retro item 2), so an arm cannot
  be configured with a string the CLI rejects.
